messages.subject: Distinct coloring of QQ plot
parts:
I've been trying to make a qq plot of my data but I having some troubles getting the coloring right. I'm plotting environmental data containing outliers. This chart is to show the whole dataset including outliers which were detected by previous tests. There is two TRUE/FALSE columns (out.irq & out.mad) corresponding to different tests. I have created a factor variable which combines the T/F into readable categories. 

When I plot the data now using color = factor(out.class), each level is plotted independently (See image 1). This makes it impossible to see the original distribution. I'm looking for a solution to color/identify the outliers on one layer without splitting them up (see image 2 highlighted points). 

This is the code I'm using: ggplot(urdb.subset, aes(sample = RESULT, colour = factor(out.class))) + geom_point(stat = "qq") 

I could try to include the data, but I would have to change it to obfuscate it.

Thank you for the help.

messages.author: d31339b95f6e694c
messages.subject: Re: Distinct coloring of QQ plot
parts:
On 2012-Mar-15, at 19:12 , evan l wrote:
>
> When I plot the data now using color = factor(out.class), each level is plotted independently (See image 1). This makes it impossible to see the original distribution. I'm looking for a solution to color/identify the outliers on one layer without splitting them up (see image 2 highlighted points).
>
> This is the code I'm using: ggplot(urdb.subset, aes(sample = RESULT, colour = factor(out.class))) + geom_point(stat = "qq")
>
> I could try to include the data, but I would have to change it to obfuscate it.

Indeed, when written this way the statistic (qq) is computed on the data split by factor level. You need to pre-compute your statistic manually and then plot it with geom_point(stat="identidy") (= geom_point()).

This should work:

urdb.subset = urdb.subset[order(urdb.subset$SAMPLE)]
urdb.subset$theoretical = qnorm(ppoints(nrow(urdb.subset))

ggplot(urdb.subset) + geom_point(aes(x=theoretical, y=subet, colour=out.class))
